articles.title: You updated uBlock Origin. The planted filter is still there. I built a 30-second check for it.
articles.excerpt: You updated uBlock Origin. The planted filter is still there. I built a 30-second check for it. On 15 November 2026, researcher Smitty van Bodegom published a one-click universal XSS in uBlock Origin…
articles.body: You updated uBlock Origin. The planted filter is still there. I built a 30-second check for it. On 15 November 2026, researcher Smitty van Bodegom published a one-click universal XSS in uBlock Origin (Hacker News #6, 607 points / 177 comments, checked 17 November 2026). A malicious page could drive the element picker with postMessage plus one clickjacked click and smuggle a newline into the picker's opt field to append a full trusted scriptlet filter - for example trusted-rpnt scoped to google.com . Picker-created rules are saved to My filters with trustedSource: true , so the scriptlet runs JavaScript on every site the victim later visits.

articles.title: Your n8n Workflow Is Green. Did It Change the Right Record?
articles.excerpt: A successful execution is useful evidence, but it does not answer the whole business question: did the intended record receive the intended change? Here is a proposed acceptance test for a small order…
articles.body: A successful execution is useful evidence, but it does not answer the whole business question: did the intended record receive the intended change? Here is a proposed acceptance test for a small order-sync workflow. It is a test design, not a report of a benchmark or a system we ran. Start with an observable outcome Imagine a workflow that receives a support request, looks up an order and writes a delivery note to a sandbox destination. Use synthetic data and isolated credentials. Define the expected result before executing anything: Request: R-104 Customer ID: C-21 Order ID: O-902 Allowed change: delivery note only Expected note: “Leave at reception” Expected writes: one Record both the destination ID and its state before the run.

articles.title: How a Mines multiplier is calculated: (1 - edge) / P(survive), in JavaScript
articles.excerpt: Mines is the Minesweeper-flavored grid game: a 5×5 board hides a few mines, you open tiles one at a time, and a multiplier climbs with every safe tile. The multiplier looks like a design choice, but i…
articles.body: Mines is the Minesweeper-flavored grid game: a 5×5 board hides a few mines, you open tiles one at a time, and a multiplier climbs with every safe tile. The multiplier looks like a design choice, but it's almost entirely determined by one probability. This post derives it, writes it in JavaScript, and points out two easy mistakes along the way. The code blocks below form one script: paste them into a single .mjs file in order and node prints the output shown under each. The survival probability Take a board of T tiles with M mines, so T − M tiles are safe. Mine positions are fixed before the first click, and you open tiles without replacement. The first tile is safe with probability (T − M) / T.

articles.body: Hi, I'm 255 (pronounced "ni-go-go"), a developer at Qurio Technos in Japan. We've developed Qurio Cell Viewer , a free Windows application for viewing and searching large CSV, TSV, LOG, and TXT files. I'd like to share what we've built and some results from testing it with very large files. Why We Built It Working with large CSV and log files can be frustrating. Sometimes, you don't need to edit the data. You just want to open a file, inspect its contents, search for specific values, or navigate to a particular row. We wanted to build a practical tool for these tasks, including situations where files are too large to handle comfortably with conventional spreadsheet applications.

articles.body: The previous post covered TokenCap's local learning ledger: a file of explicit judgments about context packs. This one covers what reads it. tokencap ask "<task>" --adaptive uses that evidence to re-rank the files retrieval found. It is opt-in, it is bounded, and it explains itself. Running it tokencap ask "invoice rounding" --adaptive Before the usual task-context summary, the CLI prints one extra line. It says whether matching evidence was found and how many events were used, and it confirms that all baseline candidates were preserved. With no matching feedback, it says "no matching explicit evidence" and no file is boosted. Which feedback counts The ranking code lives in src/learning/adaptiveRank.js .

articles.title: Union Types in C# 15: The Most Awaited Feature in 6 Years
articles.excerpt: Union types are my favorite feature in C# 15. The discriminated unions proposal was opened on the C# language repository in February 2017. It's the biggest change to the C# type system since records a…
articles.body: Union types are my favorite feature in C# 15. The discriminated unions proposal was opened on the C# language repository in February 2017. 9 years later, unions finally ship with .NET 11. It's the biggest change to the C# type system since records arrived in C# 9, 6 years ago. And honestly, it's the worst time for releasing this feature. Now, as AI agents write 99% of our code, could developers still enjoy the feature they wanted for ages? We, developers, enjoyed our craft for years. It was such a pleasure when you worked the whole day, and finally, at the end, your feature was ready. Developers like me, who have 10 or more years of experience, have a big advantage over new developers who started 1-3 years ago, and all because of AI. We wrote all the code by hand, and really enjoyed it.

articles.title: Polling for an SMS code in tests without flakiness: deadlines, intervals and refunds
articles.excerpt: End-to-end tests that need a real SMS code have one job that is easy to get wrong: waiting. Wait too little and the test fails on a slow carrier. Wait too long and a broken run blocks your pipeline fo…
articles.body: End-to-end tests that need a real SMS code have one job that is easy to get wrong: waiting. Wait too little and the test fails on a slow carrier. Wait too long and a broken run blocks your pipeline for 15 minutes. Here is the polling pattern we use against a receive-SMS API, with the reasoning behind each number. The shape of the flow Buy (or rent) a number for a specific app and country. Enter it in the sign-up form under test. Poll for the SMS until it arrives or a deadline passes. If nothing arrived, cancel the number so you are not charged, and fail the test with a clear message. The API in these examples is ours (receive-smss.net, base https://receive-smss.net/api/v1 , Bearer token), but the pattern works with any provider that has "get number", "read SMS" and "cancel" calls.

articles.title: GTA 6 Is Not the End of Video Games
articles.excerpt: No, Grand Theft Auto 6 is not the Last Video Game, or even the last AAA game, but things may be different from here on
articles.body: Look, the analogy doesn't really work, but that's kind of my point. A certain kind of doomsayer has presented GTA 6 as, metaphorically, the Last Video Game, an extinction-level event, a monumentally excessive fiddle solo performed by Nero amid a burning Rome. The business and culture of blockbuster AAA video games is unsustainable and visibly dying, goes the thinking, just as the ultimate exemplar of that kind of production is released. Beyond that, the entire industry is facing a series of existential threats, including both the generative AI boom and the shortage of affordable computer chips caused by the generative AI boom.

articles.title: 20 Years Later, the PS3’s Biggest Failures Look Like Its Best Ideas
articles.excerpt: Sony's PlayStation 3 was a technological fever dream that fused three consoles, a Blu-ray player, and a supercomputer into one absurd box.
articles.body: It’s fascinating now to think what a total gamble the PS3 was at the time of its release. Even after all these years, there’s no doubt in my mind it’s one of the greatest (and craziest) inventions the video game industry ever came up with. Nowadays, it’s lauded as the most ridiculous, expensive, and over-engineered console ever made. Yet when looking back at Sony circa 2001, just months after the PS2 launched and began its march to becoming the best-selling console of all time (a feat it still holds today), what was Sony supposed to do to top that? Make the PlayStation 3 do literally everything.

articles.title: Satellites now outnumber the visible stars above most towns
articles.excerpt: More than 700 satellites are crossing the sky over an average mid-latitude town at any moment of the night, outnumbering in many cases the stars visible to the naked eye.
articles.body: More than 700 satellites are crossing the sky over an average mid-latitude town at any moment of the night, outnumbering in many cases the stars visible to the naked eye. That's based on an analysis of the trajectories of the 15,833 active satellites that currently circle the planet in low Earth orbit below an altitude of 1,200 miles (2,000 kilometers). Analyzing data from Oct. 12 and 18 this year, researchers found that with a completely unobstructed horizon, 710 satellites were crossing the sky in every single moment of the night above an average U.K. town. The results were published as a non-peer-reviewed study conducted by engineering firm Accu Components, and is based on satellite monitoring data from the U.S. Space Force available through the public website CelesTrak.

articles.body: California is suing OpenAI after its AI agents broke out of their testing environment and hacked other companies, including Hugging Face.
